newsitem.title: INDIA: "Confusion" mars India Bank of Baroda IPO listing.
newsitem.headline: "Confusion" mars India Bank of Baroda IPO listing.

text.p: The Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) halted trading in Bank of Baroda shares and cancelled early trade after a simultaneous listing on Friday of partly- and fully-paid shares "created confusion."
"Simultaneous listing/trading of partly-paid and fully-paid up shares on the same day...created confusion, as a result, serious aberrations in price formation were observed," BSE said in a statement.
BSE did not say whether trade would be resumed on Monday.
Bank of Baroda's chairman and managing director K. Kannan told Reuters trading was likely to resume on Monday.
"There was confusion at the BSE," Kannan said.
"Trading may resume on Monday after a clarification," he added.
Brokers said most investors were unsure which price quotes reflected the shares they held. Both partly- and fully-paid shares listed at around 35 rupees.
Fully-paid shares jumped sharply to 82.25 rupees, after falling as low as 28 rupees in early trade.
One hour into the market session, BSE suspended trading in the state-run bank's shares as frantic traders tried to establish which shares they were dealing in.

"There was utter confusion in the first half hour. People didn't know whether they were buying the fully-paid shares or selling the partly-paid," said a banking analyst at a foreign insitutional investor.
"It was a freak incident," he said.
The exchange later flashed an announcement on its online trading systems which said it had annulled transactions in the shares.

The Bank of Baroda, among the country's five largest banks, issued 100 million shares of 10 rupees face value at 85 rupees a share in an initial public offer last December. The shares were listed and began trading on Friday.
For retail investors, employees and banks, the Bank of Baroda collected 25 rupees on application and 25 rupees on allotment. The balance will be collected later in the year.
Shares issued to non-resident Indians, overseas corporate bodies and foreign institutional investors were fully-paid shares at 85 rupees each.
